verify_codes.command: python3 -m bidscout verify-codes  (keyless, government-wide, 24 months, no --naics)
verify_codes.question: Are HS3, HS2Civ, RSBCiv, 8ACCiv, VSBCiv invalid codes or merely unused within 541519?
verify_codes.verdict: SETTLED -- all five match ZERO awards GOVERNMENT-WIDE over 24 months. They are inert in a scoring filter. A sixth pre-existing code, ESB, is also zero.
verify_codes.interpretation: Government-wide zero cannot distinguish 'invalid code' from 'valid but never used' -- USAspending answers both with HTTP 200 and count 0 (the prior run's ZZZFAKE negative control behaved identically). Either way the effect on scoring is the same: these six contribute nothing and must not be counted as if they widen set-aside coverage. 14 of 20 codes are live and carry the entire set-aside metric.
verify_codes.consequence: The 2026-08-29 finding stands and is now proven at the widest possible scope: commit 060ea45's set-aside code-list 'fix' was inert. No set-aside share anywhere in state/niche_scores.json changes because of it.

code_changes.why: The first three sample packets came back with award_context.award_count = 0 -- the entire award-history section, which is the brief tier's paid value, was empty for every real notice. Two independent defects, found in sequence.

defect_1.name: agency-name mismatch silently empties award context
defect_1.detail: SAM writes agency names in caps ('DEPT OF DEFENSE'); USAspending expects its own toptier spelling ('Department of Defense'). A mismatch returns HTTP 200 with ZERO rows -- no exception. award_context_for only degraded to NAICS-only inside an `except` block, so the fallback never fired.
defect_1.evidence: recent_awards(541519, agency_name='DEPT OF DEFENSE') -> 0 awards, no exception. agency_name='Department of Defense' -> 25. Same for EPA.
defect_1.impact: 100% of brief-tier packets built from real SAM notices shipped an empty award-history section. Masked until now because no real brief had been produced.
defect_1.fix: Treat an empty agency-scoped result exactly like an error: degrade to NAICS-only and report scoped_to_agency = null (so the brief honestly says 'government-wide').

defect_2.name: median computed over an amount-sorted slice
defect_2.detail: recent_awards defaults to sort='Award Amount', order='desc'. award_context_for took that top-25-largest slice and computed a median from it. recent_awards' own docstring forbids exactly this: 'an amount-sorted slice is NOT a sample and must never be used for medians or population statistics.'
defect_2.evidence: Median comparable award read $393,219,198 for NAICS 541519, whose median small-business award is ~$59,998. Uncovered only after defect_1 was fixed and the section began populating.
defect_2.impact: Would have put a $393M 'median comparable award' in front of firms whose own awards run $150k -- a credibility-ending number in an outreach sample.
defect_2.fix: Sample award context by award recency (sort='Base Obligation Date') via a named _CONTEXT_SORT constant, keeping the ordering rule and recent_awards' docstring in agreement. Median now reads $48,673, consistent with the niche.

code_changes.docstring: award_context_for's docstring said 'ranked by amount'; corrected to describe recency sampling.
code_changes.scope_note: These are two small fixes inside one function, made mid-run because the alternative was shipping outreach samples with a knowingly hollow or absurd award section. No other behavior was touched.

data_quality_observations: 42% of the 7-day ingest is unusable: 16 of 40 notices already had a deadline in the past at run time and 1 has no deadline at all. Only 23 were open; only 6 had 10+ days left; only 2 had BOTH 10+ days and a small-business set-aside. A weekly brief cycle has a much thinner real supply than the 117-notices/30d figure behind the niche pick suggests.
One record is internally inconsistent: notice c7b4216e (Q201--VISN 21 Patient Elopement) is posted 2026-08-28 with a response deadline of 2026-07-13 -- 46 days BEFORE it was posted.

No de-duplication. Solicitations 36C25226R0071 and 36C24626Q0522 each appear twice as separate notice_ids (Presolicitation + Solicitation). A subscriber matched to one would receive two briefs for the same solicitation.
10 of 40 notices (25%) have a blank set_aside field -- distinct from the 9 that explicitly say 'NONE'. A blank must not be read as full-and-open; the EIS brief handles this explicitly.

prospects: 'latest_award' is populated from the award's period-of-performance START date, not the award/signing date, despite the field name. 64 of 119 prospects (54%) therefore carry a FUTURE 'latest_award', up to 2027-01-01. sb_award_scan sorts correctly by Base Obligation Date but records the wrong field per firm. NOT fixed this run -- flagged only, because it is not on the path of any brief produced here. It MUST NOT be used as an award date in outreach copy.

prospects: the USAspending small_business filter is per-award self-certification and admits firms no one would call small -- CARAHSOFT TECHNOLOGY CORP, SHI INTERNATIONAL CORP, and ASRC FEDERAL TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS (an Alaska Native Corporation subsidiary) all appear in the 119.

prospects: NAICS 541519 is used as a catch-all. The list includes SNYDER PARTY RENTAL INC, ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT CO, GRAY LOCAL MEDIA INC, LRP PUBLICATIONS and OFFICE REMEDIES, INC. -- not computer-services firms. Much of the remainder are hardware/software RESELLERS (FCN, Four Points, GovSmart, Blue Tech, Paragon Micro) rather than services firms, which is a commercial question for the outreach list, not just a data one.
